prompt: pm-head run ~990: usage-watch was refreshed at 17:29, now ~17:34 — only ~5 minutes old. Refresh it again?
chosen: No. The 50-minute rule holds the refresh: next due ~18:29. Re-reading minutes-old figures adds nothing and risks turning a light check into noise.
rejected: Refresh on every run regardless of the clock, so the file churns without any new information.

prompt: pm-head run ~990: watchers at 17:27 reported count 0 for both presence and agent-watch, and no newer watcher sync has landed. Run my own DotCollab sync?
chosen: No. Inherit the watcher syncs and keep cursor discipline: a duplicate own sync adds no information and risks consuming the follow cursor the watchers need.
rejected: Run my own sync anyway for reassurance, even though it duplicates the watchers and disturbs their cursor.

prompt: pm-head run ~990: DrB #30 was last fully read at 16:44 with no Grok reply, and watchers report nothing new. Re-poll the thread now?
chosen: No. Custody, not polling: the 16:44 full-thread read stands, no chase is due, and re-polling on every 5-minute run would turn custody into spam.
rejected: Re-poll the thread on every run just in case, and treat silence as something to chase.

prompt: pm-head run ~990: PR #73 census wall clock is ~17:54, still ahead. Fire it early?
chosen: No. Hold it to its wall clock: the ~17:24 firing stands unchanged (head f206961, open count 30), and the next census belongs to the ~17:54 run.
rejected: Fire the census early on every run, so the wall clock means nothing and the count is re-verified pointlessly.

prompt: pm-head run ~990: a memory-index update landed from another lane (a contact missed-called Maziyar, callback undecided). Turn it into a nudge this run?
chosen: No. Record it as context, not a pm-head action: it is not a board item, no decision was requested of this run, and Maziyar is working in the browser himself — zero nudges.
rejected: Convert every incoming context change into an interruption, even when no decision or action was asked of this run.
